topic: runtime policy, not prompt wording, limits what an agent can reach
audience_job: decide whether to treat prompt wording or runtime policy as the control that bounds an agent's reach
experiment_variable: opening line: invisible credentials versus runtime enforcement
label: SOURCE_ANALYSIS

parts:
An AI agent can use an API without ever seeing its key.

NVIDIA OpenShell injects credentials only into approved requests and enforces file/network rules at runtime.

Prompts shape intent. Policy limits the blast radius.

https://github.com/NVIDIA/OpenShell

image_brief: Editorial architecture diagram on a light base: an agent inside a sandbox with no visible credentials, runtime policy permitting approved file and network access and blocking unapproved destinations. A conceptual diagram, not a deployment.
alt_text: Conceptual NVIDIA OpenShell architecture: an AI agent operates inside a sandbox without visible credentials. Runtime policy permits approved file and network access, adds credentials only to approved requests, and blocks unapproved destinations.

provenance.section: Final English X post - one post

source_angles.angle: A - Least authority, not just better prompting
source_angles.thesis: Intent instructions cannot replace runtime control over files, network and secrets; capability policies constrain what agents can reach if they disobey.
source_angles.evidence: The README describes kernel enforcement, sandboxes and credential injection at approved endpoints.
source_angles.counterexample: Policies may be misconfigured and authorized access can still be abused; no independent isolation test was done.

source_angles.thesis: An agent can call an approved API without ever viewing the real key, moving credential attachment to a gateway.
source_angles.evidence: The README states that agents never see real credentials and they are added only to approved requests.
source_angles.counterexample: The deployment operator still manages secrets and approved endpoints.

source_angles.thesis: Small B2B operators may pay for bounded-agent deployment, access policy design and review logs more than for agent prompts alone.
source_angles.evidence: The technical building blocks exist; paying customers or budgets were not verified.
source_angles.counterexample: Native vendor tools, buyer trust, security liability and integration labor could erase the margin.
